transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because work has been really getting to me lately. We got a new operations manager, and he’s been picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. Since then I just can’t seem to leave it at work. I come home wound up, I snap at my husband, and then I’m lying awake replaying meetings in my head. The next day I’m second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make without any trouble.
Have you been feeling anxious?

Yes, I think so. It’s mostly tied to work. Since the new operations manager started questioning how I do my inspections, I feel wound up a lot, and I keep replaying those meetings in my head even after I’m home. Then I go in the next day second-guessing calls I used to make easily.
Is there anything else in your life, besides work, that makes you feel anxious?

Not really. It mostly comes back to work and that new manager picking apart my inspection procedures. That’s what follows me home—I’m wound up, I snap at my husband, and I lie there replaying what happened. Then I go back in and second-guess things I used to do without much thought.
Do you find yourself having persistent, intrusive thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Yes, mostly about work. I keep replaying those meetings with the new operations manager in my head, especially after I get home. It’s like I can’t just shut it off, and then I start second-guessing the quality calls I’ve always made without much trouble.
Are you having trouble enjoying activities you normally like to do outside of work?

Yeah, I guess so. Evenings used to be easier for me, just our usual routine at home, but lately I’m not keeping up with that like I used to. My husband and I have been arguing more too, so it’s harder to enjoy being home and doing the normal things after work.
Have you been avoiding certain tasks or situations at work since the new operations manager started?

Yes. I’ve been pulling back from meetings I’m supposed to attend, and I’m not getting through things the way I used to. My work record has taken a hit because I’ve missed some internal deadlines. It’s embarrassing, honestly. And then I bring all that stress home, and my husband and I end up arguing more. I’m not keeping up with our usual evening routine like I used to.
Do you feel like you're doing these repetitive thoughts or behaviors as a way to prevent something bad from happening?
I don’t think so. It doesn’t feel like I’m doing it to stop something bad from happening. It’s more that the thoughts just keep coming up, and I have a hard time letting them go.
Do you feel compelled to repeat certain actions or mental acts?
No, I don’t think so. I’m not doing things over and over, like checking or counting or anything like that. It’s more just the thoughts getting stuck, not really actions I feel forced to repeat.
Are you avoiding social gatherings or activities outside of work because of how you're feeling?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself avoiding things outside of work in a clear way. Most of what I’ve been aware of is tied to work.
Are you finding it harder to take care of your daily needs or responsibilities at home?

Yes, I think so. At home I’m not keeping up with our usual evening routine like I used to, and my husband and I have been arguing more. Work has been affected too — I’ve missed some internal deadlines and I’ve pulled back from meetings I’m expected to be in.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or images that you consider irrational or senseless?

I’m not sure I’d call them irrational or senseless. I do have thoughts that kind of stick with me, but they feel connected to what’s been going on, not like random images or thoughts that make no sense.
Do you have thoughts that you feel compelled to think about over and over, even when you try to stop?

Yes. Mostly it’s about work. I keep replaying the meetings with the new operations manager, especially when he picks apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years. I try to shut it off when I get home, but I’ll still be lying there going over what was said and second-guessing calls I used to make without much trouble.
Are there any thoughts that keep coming back to you that aren't about work?
Not really. I mean, I’ll worry about things at home sometimes, but the thoughts that keep looping are mostly about work. I haven’t noticed any other specific thoughts coming back like that.
Are there any thoughts that you feel compelled to think about over and over that aren't related to your job or the new operations manager?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed any thoughts like that outside of the job situation. It’s really that stuff that keeps looping for me.
Do you worry about a wide range of things in your life, or is it mostly focused on work and the issues with the new operations manager?

It’s mostly work, honestly. Since the new operations manager came in and started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, I just can’t seem to leave it there. I come home wound up, I’ll snap at my husband, and then I’m lying awake replaying meetings. Then the next day I’m second-guessing routine quality calls I used to make without much trouble.
Are you worried about things outside of work, like your health, finances, or relationships, in the same way you're worried about work?

No, not in the same way. I mean, I have normal worries about home or bills here and there, but this feels different. It’s really tied to work and the new operations manager picking apart the procedures I’ve used for years. That’s what I can’t seem to shut off when I get home.
Do you often worry about things in a way that feels excessive or uncontrollable, even when there isn't a specific problem like the one at work?
Not really, no. I don’t usually worry like that when there isn’t something specific going on. This feels more tied to the work situation than just general worrying about everything.
Do you think you would still be feeling this anxious if the issues with the new operations manager were resolved?

I don’t really know for sure, but I think if it were actually resolved, I probably wouldn’t feel this anxious. The thing is, it hasn’t ended yet—I still have to report to him, and I’m still dealing with the procedures he changed. So I haven’t had a stretch afterward where everything was settled and the anxiety just kept going on its own.
If the issues with the new operations manager were completely resolved tomorrow, do you think you would still feel anxious?

I’m not sure, honestly. I’d like to think if it were completely resolved, I’d settle down. But it hasn’t really ended yet—I still report to him and I’m still dealing with the procedures he changed. So I haven’t had a period after it was all resolved where the anxiety just kept going for months on its own.
Do you think the anxiety would stop if the issues with the new operations manager were completely resolved?

I think it probably would, but I can’t say for sure because it hasn’t really ended. I still have to report to him, and I’m still dealing with the procedures he changed. So I haven’t had any time after it was resolved where the anxiety kept going on its own for months.
